evidence: Workbook quality row 37 and its internal annotation require later dimensions to tolerate shared-app mutations. The template-identical task tests/test.sh (SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa) launches one app/database at lines 97-113 and runs gates then scored with --max-concurrent-agent 1 at lines 203-227; no between-dimension reseeding is assumed. The task tests/app_context.md:24 explicitly says the gate record remains, browser storage/generated identities are not shared, identities/revisions must be refreshed, and judges must not assume an empty library or reset data. Constraints judge.toml:25-29 creates a uniquely prefixed CW gate record, records its actual identity, and forbids exact library counts or deleting unrelated records. Render judge.toml:27 forbids durable mutations. Functional prompt.md:5,19,106-121 accepts current server data and a previously loaded startup snippet, preserves unknown gate/unrelated records, and uses distinct protocol-owned titles. Its S22 at lines 426-430 snapshots every ACTUAL pre-restart record and complete example inventory, including gate/other records, compares current fields rather than seed counts or hardcoded IDs, then writes using the loaded current revision. S23 and S24 at lines 438-455 record actual revisions and refresh after unexpected mutations. Functional judge.toml:364-378 agrees with these state-relative expectations. Polish prompt.md:19-21,34,45-49 accepts current/empty library states, reads current state, creates its own recognisable harmless fixture, and never depends on another dimension's generated identity. Visual prompt.md:39-46,59-60 accepts the present content and legitimate empty states and performs no durable mutations. Both corresponding judge files contain no pristine-count, seed-title, fixed-ID, initial-theme or old-revision demands. Adversarial reasoning: a broken library loader that always selects the first saved record cannot use an earlier gate record to satisfy Polish navigation, because P02 requires the newly authored control's own title and source to appear. A conforming alternative using opaque IDs, a populated library and restoration of its last saved snippet at startup is accepted by the stated current-identity, recorded-content and startup alternatives; no row-37 false failure was found. These are source counterexample checks, not executed weak-app score measurements. Supplemental raw evidence: verified all 102 current_golden artifact SHA256 values in raw-evidence-index.json (index hash at review 0ce9a42ec24081625d883e612da454dd619a63d492eec16f3af5588cd13b1cc6). post-results.json SHA256 c6643004926913c89df7cac102412e49236f4416598e1ac1a4e8082d37c7e945 binds the current functional prompt/judge hashes and records all six actual pre-restart records unchanged after restart, then Primary revision 2->3 with unrelated_exact=true. launch_workflow.py:85-105 runs the later surface probe on that continuing server. surface-results.json SHA256 375f64d64ae6c71aab79e1eec4aa0ab58d975408ef9cb53c2df9bb0274525c11 records gate ID 12, the recognisable keyboard control, and a workspace containing 13 saved snippets; the keyboard route uses no pointer. This independently supports operation with prior mutations, but the script runs its gate/surface checks after functional work and is not the exact configured judge order. The source-contract check passes. No new Docker probe was needed. Configured judge completion/reward, Oracle grade and model score remain unmeasured and are not inferred from this scripted evidence.
